issues.issue: Did the officer breach procedural fairness by relying on extrinsic evidence (English skills an advantage in Korea) without letting the applicants respond?
issues.applicant_position: Officer relied on undisclosed extrinsic evidence that English skills would help the children, without putting it to the applicants.
issues.respondent_position: Officer's English-skills point was common-sense opinion, not extrinsic evidence, and was not used against the applicants.
issues.result_quote: The Officer was required to put whatever information she relied on for this conclusion to the Applicants and to give them an opportunity to respond.

issues.issue: Did the officer apply the wrong best-interests-of-the-child test for the minor applicants?
issues.applicant_position: Officer asked only whether the children could readjust to Korea, not what was in their best interests, and ignored their time in Canada.
issues.respondent_position: Officer applied the correct test; children are now adults, so a best-interests analysis was immaterial and no error arises.
issues.result_quote: In this case, the Officer focused on whether Min Ji would be able to adjust to life in South Korea without applying the appropriate test for her best interests.

issues.issue: Did the officer apply an incorrect H&C test, treating the children's situation as a hardship test?
issues.applicant_position: Officer assessed the hardship the children would face on removal and blamed them for the family's status, which is inappropriate.
issues.respondent_position: Officer applied both the best-interests test and the usual unusual, undeserved or disproportionate hardship test, which is reasonable.
issues.result_quote: Nor do I think the Officer, as alleged by the Applicants, blames the children for this situation and subjects them to an unusual and undeserved or disproportionate hardship test.

issues.issue: Was the officer's establishment analysis unreasonable (positive factors not set out, status and work counted against them)?
issues.applicant_position: Officer did not set out positive establishment factors and treated them as negatives, failing to weigh relative gain.
issues.respondent_position: Officer gave appropriate weight to all factors; applicants merely disagree with the weighting, which the Court should not reweigh.
issues.result_quote: concludes, reasonably in my view, that a return to South Korea will not subject them to unusual and undeserved or disproportionate hardship.

issues.issue: Was the officer's finding that the minor applicants could return to Canada on student visas unreasonable?
issues.applicant_position: Return on student visas is uncertain because of removal orders; officer ignored this and the likelihood of obtaining a visa.
issues.respondent_position: Reasonable finding; the applicants can apply for a study permit at any time.
issues.result_quote: the Officer was wrong to say they could return to Canada in this way.
